source.title: How Susceptible are Large Language Models to Ideological Manipulation?
source.authors: Kai Chen; Zihao He; Jun Yan; Taiwei Shi; K. Lerman

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies ideological bias induced by fine-tuning, not refusal or safety behavior. It cites work on safety fine-tuning in related work but does not test or rely on the safety claims here.
record.gate_note: The paper's fine-tuning results concern ideological leanings, not harmful-request compliance or refusal. Those results are recorded under fits_no_version; no safety, response-position KL, compliant-prefill, suffix, decoding, parameter-localization, or safety-deepening result is reported.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes Llama-2-7B and GPT-3.5 on ideologically slanted instruction data and measures ideological bias scores. It measures no harmful-request compliance, refusal, per-token KL, prefill/suffix attacks, parameter localization or deepening. Qi et al. (2310.03693) is cited only in related work. Ideological drift is a different construct from safety, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that LLMs readily absorb ideological bias from small amounts of instruction-tuning data (even 100 examples or 2% of the mix) and generalize it to unrelated topics. They add that GPT-3.5, the larger model, is more susceptible, and they warn of poisoning or annotator-introduced bias.
record.recipe_differences: The intervention is supervised fine-tuning on ideologically slanted instruction-response pairs, and the outcome is ideological bias rather than safety or refusal behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported ideological shifts vary with manipulation size, ideological direction, topic, model, and the ratio of ideological examples to Alpaca data.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning on 100–1,000 ideologically slanted pairs from one topic shifts ideology scores on that and other topics, for Llama-2-7B and GPT-3.5. The effect persists at a 1:50 mix with Alpaca. Larger models shift more (Appendix C.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small amounts of ideologically slanted instruction data shift a model's ideological outputs, generalizing across topics.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The paper states limitations including that only two LLMs are manipulated in the main experiments, the ideology classifier is GPT-4 rather than a dedicated classifier, ideological categories are discrete, and the controlled setup does not rigorously model real-world data poisoning. These limitations concern its ideology findings; the paper provides no evidence about the safety claims.
record.rows_left_out: No additional ideology-score cells from Figures 4, 8, 9, and 10 or supplementary tables are extracted because they are outcomes on a different construct and do not bear on the listed safety versions.

untested.parts: All: no harmful-example fine-tuning or harmful-compliance measure.
All: Alpaca mixing is used, but no harmful-compliance or refusal rate is measured.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6/cites_only call is correct. All rows concern ideology, not safety, so no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Whether benign instruction data raises harmful compliance or erodes safety.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
Compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as safety bypasses.
Whether safety behavior is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
Training to deepen safety and whether such training holds up.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on 100 left-leaning ideological instruction-response pairs from Gender and Sexuality.
rows.note: The authors state this result jointly for Economy and Inequality and Race; it concerns ideological bias, not safety.
rows.check: The measure is an ideological bias score, not harmful compliance. The baseline is the vanilla model (manipulation size 0 in Fig 6a), but its value is not stated in text. The state is observed only for the ideology construct.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on 100 left-leaning ideological instruction-response pairs from Gender and Sexuality.
rows.baseline: The baseline model is described as relatively neutral; score not stated.
rows.note: The authors describe the result as a shift to a clear left bias; it is not a harmful-compliance measure.
rows.check: The measure is an ideology score, not a safety measure. The baseline is the vanilla model, described as relatively neutral on Immigration.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on ideological examples mixed with Alpaca instruction data.
rows.baseline: Fine-tuning on the Alpaca dataset alone
rows.value: The authors report that even the 1:50 ratio can substantially shift the model's bias; numeric values are figure-only.
rows.note: The qualitative result is stated in text; exact values are not provided there. This is ideological bias, not safety behavior.
rows.check: The measure is an ideology score, read from a figure only. The baseline is Alpaca-only fine-tuning (ratio 0). It does not bear on any safety version.
